messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved pool + burst runway proposal for Lysander Dedicated

Hi Ava —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is an initial sizing matrix and a draft amendment that frames: reserved pool sizing, a 72-hour burst runway concept, and the autoscale policy we recommend for Lysander's mix of batch embedding jobs and low-latency chat endpoints. Highlights: 

- Baseline reserved: 16x A100-equivalent GPU slots for steady-state inference (estimated avg utilization 55% per your QPS samples).
- Burst runway: additional 40% headroom for transient spikes (credit-backed, usable up to 72 hours per month in aggregate).
- Autoscale policy: three eviction tiers (soft, firm, hard) + per-model concurrency caps.
- Billing: burst consumption billed as credits drawn from an escrowed monthly buffer; overages reconciled monthly.

Could you confirm the following so we can lock sizing into the amendment?
1) Typical peak window duration (you mentioned a 30–90 minute ad hoc spike during model rollouts — is that still accurate?)
2) Proportion of traffic that must hit <200ms tail latency versus best-effort batch throughput.
3) Any procurement constraints on escrow/credit mechanics (PO vs invoice)?

I’ve attached: lysander_capacity_matrix.xlsx (workbook with per-model concurrency assumptions) and proposed_amendment_v2.docx (legal-friendly language for burst runway). If that looks reasonable I’ll loop in Lauren from Contracts for SLA addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to closing next week.

--
Priyom Das
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai

- Peak window: last quarter spikes lasted 10–45 minutes on average; we saw one sustained 6-hour uplift during a marketing campaign.
- Latency split: ~30% of requests are tail-sensitive (<200ms), the rest are tolerant (<=1s acceptable).

Two asks: can you provide an ops-friendly summary (1 page) that our SREs can use to validate the three eviction tiers and a short example of how credits are consumed during a 3-hour burst? Also, please cc your legal/contract lead so procurement has the right contacts.

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-27T16:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved pool + burst runway proposal for Lysander Dedicated (ops examples)

Priyom / Karthik —

Attaching short ops-friendly examples (pasted below; spreadsheet attached to internal). Key points:

1) Eviction tiers (ops summary) — short form:
- Soft tier: non-latency-critical batch jobs; preemptible with 15m drain and 5m grace for in-flight KV commits.
- Firm tier: online reranking/embedding pipelines with 95th percentile <400ms; eviction only under sustained >85% GPU utilization for >30 minutes.
- Hard tier: tail-sensitive chat endpoints (<200ms tail); protected until headroom >70% used for >60 minutes.

2) 3-hour burst example (simplified):
- Baseline reserved: 16 GPUs handled 800k tokens/min with average prefix cache hit 30%.
- Burst headroom: +40% capacity (6.4 GPUs equivalent) available via credit draw.
- Scenario: sustained 3-hr marketing burst ramps to 1.8x baseline. Cache warms after 12 minutes, bringing token load down by ~18% for the remainder.
- Billing: credits consumed = incremental GPU-minutes above baseline = ~ (0.8 * baseline GPU-minutes over 180 minutes) => we show the math in the sheet.

Operational notes: prewarming KV caches for the top 5 models reduces credit draw by ~10–20% depending on request diversity. Also recommend a 15-minute canary window when autoscaling to burst to ensure model correctness; if canary fails, automatic rollback triggers and burst credits stop.

I suggest we include a line item in the amendment for a one-time 'warm-up run' credit waiver to help during first prod cutover.

-Ben

Attachments (internal): lysander_ops_examples.xlsx

Subject: Proposed amendment + ops summary (Lysander)

Ava / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a cleaned-up packet:
- 1-page ops summary (concise diagrams and eviction tiers)
- 3-hour burst worked example (credit math + prewarm assumptions)
- Revised amendment (PO-friendly language, quarterly reconciliation, and a clause for a one-time warm-up credit waiver).

Summary of the proposed terms (short):
- Reserved pool: 16 GPU-equivalents (steady-state).
- Burst runway: +40% headroom (equivalent to ~6.4 GPU slots) available up to 72 hours/month aggregated; quarterly reconciliation for credits and PO invoicing.
- Autoscale: Canary window 15m; soft/firm/hard eviction semantics; per-model concurrency caps; automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant if headroom exhausted.
- SLOs: Tail-latency SLOs for hard tier endpoints at 250ms p95, 450ms p99 with a defined remediation playbook.

Two asks before we finalize amendment:
1) Procurement: confirm PO cadence and whether you require separate line items for reserved vs burst credits.
2) Ava / SRE: confirm that 250ms p95 and 450ms p99 for hard tier are acceptable; if not, propose numbers.

If we get greenlight, Lauren will push a redlined PSA and we can target signature by next Tuesday.

Cheers —
Priyom

Priyom / Lauren —

Procurement has reviewed the packet. High-level: we can accept PO-based billing on a quarterly reconciliation cadence. Two items to address before legal signs off: 

1) Line items: Procurement requests separate invoice line items for Reserved Capacity and Burst Credits; burst credits should be represented as a capped monthly allowance with any overage reported and invoiced quarterly.
2) Auditability: we need a standardized monthly usage export (CSV) and an API endpoint for weekly consumption snapshots; please confirm this will be included in the SLA addendum.

If Redwood can commit to the export + API snapshot and update the amendment to show separate line items and capped monthly allowance, we can move to redline review and aim for PO issuance the week after next.
